newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end softer with cash market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end softer with cash market.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended weaker on Tuesday as the underlying cash market gave way after a rapid drop in dollar/yen.
Dealers said an initial firm tone of the Toyko stock market caught many off-guard, as the stance had been to wait for direction from Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
But speculation the U.S. would leave interest rates unchanged at the FOMC meeting, while Japanese politicians were calling for higher Japanese rates, caused the yen to firm.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended down 195 points at 20,345, on a moderately active volume of 16,000 lots.
"The tables were being turned on interest rate speculation. People thought the gap would close between the U.S. and Japan," a dealer with a European commission house said.
Export-oriented stocks in the cash market suffered losses on concerns Japan's trade surplus with the U.S. would worsen.
Dealers said that a year-on-year rise in Japan's April-June industrial production, up 6.5 percent, also hurt sentiment.
Meanwhile, the dollar fell to 112.80 yen in late Tokyo.
On SIMEX Taiwan futures, May shed 5.9 points to 342.9, tracking losses in the stock market.
